title: Fu Hao
summary: Fu Hao was a consort of the Shang king Wu Ding. Oracle bone inscriptions are said to name her as a general in several military campaigns, and she is also said to have presided over sacrifices. Her tomb at Anyang, excavated in 1976, held more than 1,600 objects, including 468 bronzes with 130 weapons, and is described as the only unlooted tomb of a Shang royal family member found.

uncertainty.note: The pages date her tomb, not her life: University of Washington says "around 1250 BC", EBSCO says "c. 1200 B.C.E." The range spans both.

where.modern_name: Tomb of Fu Hao, Yinxu (Yin Ruins), Anyang, Henan, China (pinned to her excavated tomb at Anyang)
where.historical_name: Yin, the late Shang capital near present Anyang, under King Wu Ding

importance.justification: University of Washington and EBSCO describe her as a royal consort whose intact tomb yielded the largest jade assemblage and hundreds of bronzes, with oracle bone evidence of military command.

reviewer_note: Dates are for the tomb and conflict between sources (c. 1250 vs c. 1200 BC).
